title: Practice: bounds in calculations
intro: Ask what makes the answer as big — or as small — as possible.

questions.prompt: $a = 7.2$ and $b = 3.6$, both to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound of $a + b$.
$a = 7.2$ and $b = 3.6$, both to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound of $a - b$.
A square has side $6$ cm, to the nearest cm. Find the lower bound of its area.
A cyclist travels $36$ km (to the nearest km) in $1.5$ hours (to the nearest 0.1 h). Find the upper bound of her average speed, to 3 s.f.
A metal block has mass $850$ g (to the nearest 10 g) and volume $110\ \text{cm}^3$ (to the nearest $\text{cm}^3$). Find the lower bound of its density, to 3 s.f.
$p = 12$ and $q = 4$, both to the nearest whole number. Which gives the **lower bound** of $\frac{p}{q}$?

questions.scenario: A rectangular field is $120$ m by $85$ m, both to the nearest 5 m. A square of side $20$ m, to the nearest metre, is fenced off for a garden.

steps.prompt: Upper bound of the area of the whole field.
steps.hint: To the nearest 5 m, so ± 2.5 m.

steps.prompt: Lower bound of the area of the garden.
Upper bound of the area left for grazing.

questions.explanation: Upper bound of the grazing area = UB(field) − LB(garden) $= 10\,718.75 - 380.25 = 10\,338.5\ \text{m}^2$.
